name: cloud-contacts
description: Diego's Cloud Contacts — standalone Android multi-channel people hub. NOT a dialer-first address book: each person is a set of reachable CHANNELS (WhatsApp, Telegram, SMS, Cloud Mail, Cloud Dialer, Matrix, Cloud Chat, LinkedIn, Instagram) and the person screen is a channel switchboard — tapping a channel opens that conversation in its app; there is no default call action. Sources merged into one identity: device contacts (local phone + synced accounts such as Gmail) read from ContactsContract, plus LinkedIn Connections.csv and Instagram followers/following JSON imports parsed natively. WebView UI over HTML/Tailwind (cloud-news pattern). Build via Nix devShell, one APK out.

channels._doc: THE data-driven multi-channel registry — the app's whole identity. Baked into app BuildConfig as CHANNELS_B64 (app/build.gradle) and rendered by libs:contacts Channels + the switchboard UI. Adding a channel is a JSON edit, never Kotlin. kind decides which person datum makes the channel available and feeds its URI placeholders: 'phone' (any phone; {phone}=raw, {phone_digits}=digits-only E.164-ish), 'email' ({email}), 'url:<domain>' (a website containing <domain>; {url}), 'handle:<key>' (person.handles[<key>]; {handle}). package is a soft hint — the bridge tries it first, then falls back to the system chooser, so absent constellation apps degrade gracefully. order drives switchboard sorting; no channel is a default action by design.

auto_update._doc_max_installs_per_pass: Most install sessions ONE unattended background pass may open. A background pass cannot show the system install dialog (Android 10+ blocks background activity starts), so each install it starts leaves a tap-to-install notification holding a PackageInstaller session until the user answers it. Unbounded, one pass over the 40-entry fleet opens 40 and the installer hits Android's 50-session cap - 'Too many active sessions for UID'. The remainder is picked up by the next pass. User-initiated 'Update all' is NOT capped: it runs in the foreground where the dialog appears and sessions resolve at once.

analytics._doc: Consumed by :libs:analytics, which reads THIS file (rootDir) at build time and bakes the values into BuildConfig. Both backends are single-site today, so every app reports into the same site and is told apart by .app — give each app its own site_id once per-app sites exist in Umami/Matomo.

ui._doc: #1164 THE navigation declaration (libs:bottomnav NavDecl) of the contacts.html WebView shell: ui.bottom_nav is the shared bottom nav, each section is one page of the web UI and a tap runs its switchTab(). The first row (Profile top-right opens Cloud Account) and the scroll-collapse are the shared libs'; the WebView's scroll feeds the one collapse connection.

configs_pages._doc: Configs > General and Configs > About (libs:ui-nav-bars fleetconfigs, rule 1_cicd/src/data/configs-pages.json, #1352 v2). general.sections: the anchors of the one General page, in order (perms, battery, storage, notifications, ui, language are required; app opens this app's own Configs; update is added after perms by default). about: the hand-written part of the extensive About: tagline, description, features, screens, guide, privacy, backends (ids of ac_cloud-account/build.json::fleet_endpoints, resolved to mesh URLs at build time), related fleet apps, credits for a fork. Permissions, data stores, crash/analytics libs, name, icon, version, build sha and date, repo, licence, origin, crash sink, debug API and changelog are derived, never typed here.

about.tagline: People as channels, one tap to reach them
about.description: Cloud Contacts is a people hub rather than an address book: each person is the set of channels you can reach them on — WhatsApp, Telegram, SMS, Cloud Mail, Cloud Dialer, Matrix, Cloud Chat, LinkedIn, Instagram — and the person screen is a switchboard that opens the right app on the right conversation in one tap. It exists because most contact is no longer a phone call, and the phone's own contacts app does not know that.
features: People with every channel: WhatsApp, Telegram, SMS, mail, calls, Matrix
One tap to the right app per channel

guide: Grant Contacts so the hub can read the phone's contacts.
Open a person and tap a channel to start talking there.
Use Import to add people from other sources.
about.privacy: No ads and no third-party trackers. A crash report is saved on the phone and sent only to the phone's own C3 WebServer over loopback; nothing leaves the device unless you share it. Usage analytics are opt-in and off by default; when allowed, events go only to the owner's self-hosted Umami and Matomo. It calls no fleet service: its data stays on the phone.

perms._doc: #1360 every grant this app needs, by libs:perms catalogue id (needs), and the fleet apps that do work for it with the grants THEY must hold (helpers). The ONE declaration: generated into assets/app-perms.json (cloud-android-perms-guard.py --write), drawn by Configs > General > Perms (libs:perms AppPermsSection) with live state, Grant / Open and Grant all, asked at first run (first_run), and reported as 'Missing permission X - Grant' when an operation fails (PermsGate). perms-guard fails when code uses a gated API or another app's engine that is not declared here, or when the manifest and this list disagree.
